title: Responses to Iron Limitation in Hordeum vulgare L. as Affected by the Atmospheric CO2 Concentration
authors: Haase, Rothe, Kania, Wasaki, Romheld, Engels, Kandeler, Neumann
notes: Two experiments: hydroponic culture and soil (rhizobox) culture. Only soil culture reported Fe concentration data. Fe content (total per shoot) increased 47-52% under elevated CO2, but Fe CONCENTRATION was not significantly affected (dilution by increased biomass). Only Fe was measured as mineral element. Data from Fig. 3a (Fe content) and Fig. 3b (Fe concentration).

consensus_observations.treatment_description: elevated CO2 (800 umol/mol), +Fe (20 umol Fe/kg soil as Fe-EDTA), soil culture, 28 DAS
consensus_observations.control_description: ambient CO2 (400 umol/mol), +Fe (20 umol Fe/kg soil as Fe-EDTA), soil culture, 28 DAS

consensus_observations.treatment_description: elevated CO2 (800 umol/mol), -Fe (no Fe supply), soil culture, 28 DAS
consensus_observations.control_description: ambient CO2 (400 umol/mol), -Fe (no Fe supply), soil culture, 28 DAS
